examples.title: A cup for fresh cacao

original.creator: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
original.note: Carved hieroglyphs run diagonally across the back. Gift of Justin Kerr and Dicey Taylor, 2017.

translation.text: it is his cup for fresh (or pure) cacao
translation.rightsNote: Short attributed quotation from The Met’s reading of the first half of the inscription.

examples.context: The next part of the label identifies the owner as a sajal, a member of the local nobility. The diagonal writing comes upright as the cup is tilted. The map points to the Oxkintok area, which the museum proposes as the likely region of this ceramic style.

examples.title: A lord’s name tag on a cup

original.creator: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
original.note: The owner’s name appears in the carved scene beside the seated figure. Purchase, Joseph Pulitzer Bequest, 1992.

translation.text: the drinking cup of Baje(?) Kaan (or Chan) Took', the ruler
translation.rightsNote: Short attributed quotation of The Met’s reading. The parentheses preserve uncertainty. The photograph’s CC0 dedication applies to the image.

examples.context: The inscription attaches a person’s name and title to the vessel. The seated figure’s elbow overlaps the last glyph block, so the artist made the label part of the scene. The museum’s record gives Mexico as the geographic attribution and discusses the Yucatán Peninsula. The precise origin is uncertain.

examples.title: A chocolate cup with its owner named

original.creator: Image courtesy of the Princeton University Art Museum
original.note: The museum’s rollout photograph shows the pictorial scene and the painted rim with its dedicatory text. Museum purchase, gift of the Hans A. Widenmann, Class of 1918, and Dorothy Widenmann Foundation.

translation.rightsNote: Short English rendering of the beverage designation in the museum’s catalogue.

examples.context: The rim dedicates the cup, gives the kind of chocolate it was meant to hold, and names its owner as Muwaan K’uk’. Below, a woman pours chocolate from one vessel to another to make it froth. The map shows the approximate Nakbé region where the museum places production.

examples.title: Ten pesos and four reales for a plot
examples.place: Santiago Xochac and the Coyoacán region, Mexico

original.text: tomatica oticuique . x pos . iiii to
original.creator: James Lockhart
original.note: Opening clause of the payment statement in the Early Nahuatl Library’s analytic transcription. The underlying colonial manuscript text is in the public domain. The linked edition supplies the transcription.
original.license: Short cited transcription excerpt; no open reuse license asserted

translation.text: we took in our hands 10 pesos and 4 reales
translation.rightsNote: Short attributed excerpt from a modern English translation.

examples.context: Pedro de Santiago and Toribio Silvestre confirm receiving money for their land near the Xochimilco boundary. They say the proceeds paid for two high masses for their father. The marker is at Coyoacán, the regional reference point for the sale.

sources.title: Early Nahuatl Library, Coyoacán land sale, folio a

examples.title: A mother leaves her house to Juana

original.creator: Robert Haskett
original.note: Bequest clause in the Early Nahuatl Library’s analytic transcription. Abbreviations are retained. The underlying colonial manuscript text is in the public domain. The linked edition supplies the transcription.
original.license: Short cited transcription excerpt; no open reuse license asserted

translation.text: I bequeath it all to the small child Juana.
translation.rightsNote: Short attributed excerpt from a modern English translation.

examples.context: María Ximénez says she inherited the house from her late father and gives it to her young daughter. It is followed by a list of fields. Her will survived because a descendant produced family property documents during a later dispute over tribute funds.

sources.title: Early Nahuatl Library, María Ximénez’s testament, folio 423v

examples.title: A pair of oxen left to two heirs
examples.objectId: AGEO, Alcaldías Mayores, leg. 42, exp. 10, ff. 7r–7v (Ticha Tl675b)

original.text:
tinipea toui nesabi chiña gona rosa
naya lachiña thomas martin guañe lucas
Luis
original.creator: Ticha digital text explorer for Colonial Zapotec
original.note: Excerpt from the Ticha transcription of the seventeenth-century will, with its line breaks retained. The published interlinear analysis identifies this as the bequest of a yoke of oxen.

translation.text: I order [that] one yoke of oxen, I leave in the hands of Tomás Martín and Lucas Luis
translation.translator: Pamela Munro, Kevin Terraciano, Michael Galant, Brook Danielle Lillehaugen, Xóchitl Flores-Marcial, Maria Ornelas, Aaron Huey Sonnenschein, and Lisa Sousa
translation.rightsNote: Short attributed quotation from the interlinear English translation, lines 33–35.

examples.context: Sebastiana de Mendoza’s will lists land, young maguey plants, clothing, cash, and a working pair of oxen. Tlacochahuaya is the town attached to the record in the Ticha archive catalogue.
